title: How to Check CIBIL Credit Score Free - All 4 Bureaus 2026
meta_description: Check CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF score free in 2026. RBI gives 1 free report per bureau yearly. Plus SBI YONO, bank app and fintech app routes.

hero.one_liner: Check your credit score free from all 4 bureaus: CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF. RBI mandates one free annual report from each, and your bank app shows it monthly

sections.heading: CIBIL Score Kya Hota Hai: The 3-Digit Number Deciding Your Loans
content: A credit score is a 3-digit number between 300 and 900 that tells lenders how likely you are to repay on time. It is built from your EMI history, credit card payments, defaults, and loan inquiries.

Four RBI-licensed bureaus maintain it in India: CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark. All four use the same 300-900 scale, though each may show a slightly different number because lenders report to them separately.

CIBIL is the one most banks pull, which is why everyone says CIBIL score when they mean credit score. Checking your own score never reduces it: that is a soft inquiry, and only lender checks after loan applications count as hard inquiries.

sections.title: Your RBI Right: 4 Free Reports a Year
sections.content:
Since 2017, RBI requires every credit bureau to give you one free full credit report with score each calendar year. That means 4 free reports annually across CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and CRIF.

No bureau can charge for this first report or hide it behind a subscription. If a site pushes payment before showing the free option, you are on the wrong page.

sections.heading: How to Check CIBIL Score Free on the Official Website

steps.title: Open cibil.com and pick the free option
steps.description: Go to cibil.com and click Get Free CIBIL Score & Report. Ignore the paid subscription banners: the free tier is a separate button.

steps.title: Register with PAN details
steps.description: Enter your name exactly as on PAN, your 10-digit PAN, date of birth, email, and mobile. PAN is the primary ID the bureau matches your credit history against.

steps.title: Verify with OTP
steps.description: An OTP comes to your mobile. Enter it to confirm your identity and activate the free account.

steps.title: View score and download the report
steps.description: Your score appears on the dashboard with the full report below it. Download the PDF: it lists every loan, card, payment month, and lender inquiry against your name.

sections.heading: Reading Your Report: The 4 Blocks That Matter
content: Personal information block: name, PAN, DOB, addresses. Check spelling against PAN because mismatches here are why some people see a partial or missing history.
Accounts block: every loan and card with sanctioned amount, current balance, and status code. This is where a closed loan wrongly showing active hides in plain sight.
Payment history grid: month-by-month boxes per account, where 000 means paid on time and any number is days past due. One stray 030 from two years ago explains many mystery score dips.
Enquiry block: every lender who pulled your report, with dates. An enquiry you never triggered is your earliest fraud signal, so scan this block first on every pull.

sections.heading: Experian, Equifax, CRIF: The Other 3 Free Reports
content: Experian (experian.in): click Free Credit Report, register with PAN, verify OTP, download. The process mirrors CIBIL and takes about 5 minutes.
Equifax (equifax.co.in): find Free Credit Score, register with PAN, verify with OTP. Your score and full report arrive by email within minutes.
CRIF High Mark (crifhighmark.com): choose Check Your Score, register, verify. All three use the same 300-900 scale as CIBIL, so the numbers read the same way.
Spacing trick: pull a different bureau every quarter. That gives you 4 free checkups a year without ever paying for monitoring.

sections.heading: Free vs Paid CIBIL Plans: Do You Need to Pay?
content: CIBIL sells subscriptions with unlimited score refreshes and monitoring alerts. For most people they are unnecessary because the free routes already cover everything.
The free annual report shows your complete history, bank apps refresh your score monthly at no cost, and dispute filing is free by regulation.
Paying makes sense only in one situation: you are actively repairing a damaged report and want weekly visibility while disputes resolve. Otherwise keep the money.

sections.heading: SBI, PNB, Bajaj: Checking Score Inside Apps You Already Use
content: SBI: open YONO, go to Loans & Insurance, then Credit Score. It pulls your real CIBIL score free, the same number SBI's loan desk sees.
PNB: the PNB One app shows your CIBIL score under its loans section. There is no separate PNB cibil, it is the same TransUnion CIBIL number.
HDFC, ICICI, Axis: each app has a Check Credit Score option under Loans. All free, all monthly, no registration beyond your existing login.
Bajaj Finserv and Paytm show your Experian score free, and CRED shows CIBIL. A bank app score can differ from a fintech app score because they pull from different bureaus, not because either is fake.

sections.heading: Written Off or Suit Filed on Your Report? What It Means
content: Written off means the lender stopped expecting repayment and absorbed the loss, but the debt does not vanish. The tag stays on your report for 7 years and most banks refuse fresh credit while it shows.

The only clean exit is paying the full outstanding and getting the status changed to Closed, with a No Dues Certificate from the lender. Never accept a verbal assurance: the report update is what future lenders see.
Suit filed means the lender went to court over the dues. Resolve it with the lender first, then verify the tag is removed in your next report pull.
Settled looks tempting when a lender offers to close at 60-70% of dues. It saves money today and costs you borrowing access for years, so treat it as the last resort before default, not a smart deal.

sections.heading: 5 Factors That Move Your Score

items.title: Payment history (biggest weight)
items.sub: Every EMI and card bill on time. One missed payment hurts for months.

items.title: Credit utilization
items.sub: Keep card spending under 30% of your limit. High usage signals stress.

items.title: Credit history length
items.sub: Older accounts help. Never close your oldest card.

items.title: Hard inquiries
items.sub: Each loan application costs 5-10 points temporarily. Space them out.

items.title: Credit mix
items.sub: A card plus an installment loan reads better than cards alone.

sections.heading: CIBIL Score Kaise Badhaye: The Realistic Timeline
content: Months 1-3: pay every EMI and card bill on time, and clear any overdue amount immediately. Overdue clearance is the single biggest jump, worth 30-50 points on its own.
Drop card utilization below 30% of your limit. If your limit is ₹1 lakh, keep spending under ₹30,000, and the score responds within a month or two.
Months 3-6: ask your card bank for a limit increase without raising your spending. That mechanically lowers utilization.
Do not apply for any new credit in this window. Every application is a hard inquiry, and five rejections in 3 months can cost 25-50 points plus visible rejection entries.
Months 6-12: with clean behaviour throughout, an 80-150 point recovery is a realistic range. That is enough to move from poor to good territory, though exact gains vary by profile.

sections.heading: How Often Your Score Updates (And Why Yesterday Differed)
content: Lenders report your repayment data to bureaus on a monthly cycle, and the bureau refreshes your score roughly every 30-45 days after that data lands. Your score is a moving photograph, not a fixed grade.
This is why the app showed 742 yesterday and 738 today: a new card statement, an inquiry, or a lender's monthly upload landed in between.
Small swings of 5-15 points month to month are normal noise. What matters is the 6-month trend line, not any single reading.

sections.heading: Found an Error in Your Report? Fix It Free

steps.title: Spot the error
steps.desc: Closed loan showing active, someone else's account, wrong SMA status, or a duplicate entry. All four are common and all drag your score.

steps.title: Raise a dispute at cibil.com
steps.desc: Use Raise a Dispute, select the wrong entry, describe the error, and upload proof like a closure letter or bank statement.

steps.title: Bureau verifies with lender
steps.desc: CIBIL contacts the lender within 30 days. Follow up if you hear nothing after a month.

steps.title: Correction reflects
steps.desc: If the lender confirms, the report is corrected and your score adjusts within 1-2 months. Corrections are always free and can recover 20-30 points.

sections.heading: What Your Score Actually Costs You in Rupees
content: Home loan: a 750+ score gets roughly 8.5-9% interest while 700 gets 9-9.5%. On ₹50 lakh over 20 years, that 1% gap is about ₹7.2 lakh extra interest.
At 650, large banks often reject outright, leaving housing finance companies at 10-11%. Your score decides whether the same house costs ₹85 lakh or ₹92 lakh in total repayment.
Personal loans show the widest spread: 10-11% at 750+, but 18-24% or rejection below 650. Premium credit cards need 750+, basic cards around 700, and below 650 only FD-backed secured cards remain.
Even outside banking it follows you. Metro landlords increasingly run tenant credit checks before handing over keys.

sections.title: Checking Your Own Score Has Zero Impact
sections.content:
Self-checks are soft inquiries. You can check daily through your bank app and the score will not move.

Only lender checks after you apply for a loan or card are hard inquiries, costing 5-10 points temporarily. That is the entire difference.

sections.heading: Before You Apply: Sequence It Right
content: Check your score before any application, never after. Below 750, spend 3-6 months improving first because rejected applications leave marks future lenders see.
At 700-749: try your salary bank first since the existing relationship helps, and use pre-approved offers in your banking app which run on soft inquiries.
Below 650: do not apply anywhere yet. Clear overdues, set auto-pay on everything, take a secured card to rebuild, and wait 6-12 months.
Desperate applications at low scores push people toward unregulated loan apps charging 24-36%. Patient rebuilding always beats desperate borrowing.

sections.heading: CIBIL Truths vs Myths
qualify: Self-checking is free and never lowers your score
A ₹15,000/month earner with clean payments can outscore a ₹5 lakh/month defaulter: salary is not in the formula
Responsible card use is the fastest score builder from zero
Old paid-off cards help your score: keep them open
disqualify: Myth: checking your own score reduces it
Myth: settlement is fine. A Settled tag drops 75-100 points and stays 7 years
Myth: no credit card means better CIBIL. No history means no score at all
Myth: closing paid-off cards helps. It shortens history and spikes utilization

sections.heading: Whose Loans Touch Your Score: Co-Applicant, Guarantor, Spouse
content: Co-applicant on a loan: the account sits on both reports, so every EMI, on time or late, hits both scores equally. Joint home loans make both partners' credit move together.
Guarantor: if the borrower defaults, the default lands on your report too. Standing guarantee for a relative's loan is a real credit risk, not a formality signature.
Spouse with an independent loan: no effect on you. Scores are individual and marriage does not merge them, so a partner's personal loan in their own name never shows on your report.
Add-on credit cards: all spending reports against the primary holder. If your add-on user overspends, the utilization damage is yours alone.

sections.heading: Loan Without CIBIL Score: What Actually Exists
content: If you have no score or a damaged one, unsecured personal loans from banks are mostly closed. What genuinely works is secured lending: gold loans, loans against FD, and loans against property, because the collateral replaces the score.
A loan against your own FD needs no credit check at all and costs only 1-2% above your FD rate. Gold loans from banks and regulated NBFCs run on the ornament value, not your history.
What to avoid: instant loan apps promising money with no CIBIL check. The regulated ones still check, and the unregulated ones charge 24-36% with harassment-based recovery.
If an app is not listed with an RBI-registered NBFC, the no-CIBIL promise is the bait. Check the lender name in RBI's NBFC register before touching it.

sections.heading: No Score Yet? Build One for Free
content: Fresh graduates and first-time borrowers show NH or -1: no history. The fix is a secured credit card against a fixed deposit of ₹15,000-25,000, which nearly every bank issues without a credit check.
Use it for small monthly purchases of ₹2,000-5,000 and pay the full bill every month. A score appears after about 6 months, typically in the 650-700 zone.
After 12 months of perfect payments you sit around 700-750, and the bank upgrades you to a regular card. The FD comes back to you with interest, so building credit from scratch effectively costs ₹0.

sections.heading: Zero to 750: The 12-Month Roadmap

items.desc: Fixed deposit of ₹15,000-25,000 at any bank, card issued against it with roughly 80% of the FD as limit. No credit check needed because the FD is the guarantee.
Use ₹2,000-5,000 monthly and pay the complete bill before due date every single time. Keep utilization under 30% of the limit throughout.
The NH or -1 tag turns into a real number, typically in the 650-700 zone. Check it free through your bank app to confirm reporting started.
With a clean year you sit near 700-750 and the bank offers a regular unsecured card. The FD returns with interest, making the whole build effectively free.

sections.title: Fraud Alert: Watch Who Checks You
sections.content:
Register for free alerts at cibil.com so you get an SMS whenever a lender pulls your report. An inquiry for a loan you never applied for means someone may be borrowing on your identity.

Contact that lender immediately and raise a dispute with the bureau. Early detection is the whole game with identity fraud.

sections.title: Free full reports every year
sections.desc: One from each bureau under RBI rules: CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, CRIF High Mark. Space them quarterly and you are monitored year-round for free.

sections.heading: Official Sources & References
sections.content:
Source: TransUnion CIBIL, Experian India, Equifax India, and CRIF High Mark, all regulated by RBI under CICRA 2005. Free annual report rules follow RBI's Master Direction on Credit Information Companies.

For the latest terms, check cibil.com and rbi.org.in directly.

sections.text: Your CIBIL score is the one exam you can retake every month for free. Check it before the bank does.

faqs.question: I checked my CIBIL score yesterday and today it's different. Why does it change so frequently?
faqs.answer:
Your score updates monthly (sometimes weekly) based on new credit activities: (1) EMI payments (on-time or late), (2) Credit card usage and payments, (3) New loan inquiries, (4) Settled/closed accounts. Most activity is captured by the 5th-10th of each month when lenders report data to bureaus.

Don't obsess over 10-20 point fluctuations - focus on the trend over 3-6 months.

faqs.question: Can I improve my credit score from 650 to 750 in 2 months?
faqs.answer:
Unlikely unless you have specific quick wins: (1) Pay off a large outstanding credit card balance immediately (can jump 20-30 points), (2) Correct errors in your report (can jump 10-50 points depending on error). In 2 months, realistically expect 30-50 point improvement with perfect payment behavior.

Building a 750 score typically takes 12-18 months of consistent on-time payments, low utilization, and credit mix.

faqs.question: My score is 800 but I can't get an HDFC personal loan approved. What's happening?
faqs.answer:
Credit score is just one factor. HDFC (and most banks) also verify: (1) Your monthly salary (must be at least ₹25-30K depending on loan amount), (2) Employment stability (ITR for self-employed, or 2+ years in current job for salaried), (3) Your age (must be 21-65 for most loans), (4) Existing debt (if you already have ₹5L EMI per month, can't take another ₹5L loan).

If all these check out, contact HDFC directly asking why you were rejected - they must provide a reason.

faqs.question: Is there a benefit to checking all 4 bureaus' scores or is CIBIL enough?
faqs.answer:
For most purposes, CIBIL is enough since 95% of Indian lenders use it. However, checking all 4 is good practice: (1) If CIBIL shows 700 but Experian shows 650, there's likely an error somewhere - investigate.

(2) Some lenders (small NBFCs, fintech) may check non-CIBIL bureaus - knowing your score there helps. (3) If applying for jobs/visas abroad, international bureaus matter.

In 20 minutes, check all 4 for free - it's worth it.

faqs.question: I got rejected for a credit card 3 months ago. How long does that hard inquiry impact my score?
faqs.answer:
A hard inquiry reduces your score by 5-10 points, and the impact lasts 6-12 months on your report. However, the reduction in score usually fades in 1-2 months if you make on-time payments.

By 3 months, the impact is minimal (5-10 points reduction). Wait 2-3 months between hard inquiries to minimize cumulative impact.

faqs.question: My parents died and I inherited their debt. Will it affect my credit score?
faqs.answer:
No. Credit liability is personal - you're not legally responsible for deceased parents' debt unless you co-signed the loan.

The inherited debt stays on their (deceased's) name/PAN and doesn't affect your score. However, if you take a personal loan to pay off inherited debt, that new loan affects your score.

Check your credit report to ensure no errors showing inherited loans under your name - if there are, dispute them immediately.

faqs.question: My husband applied for a loan under his name only. Did that affect my credit score?
faqs.answer:
No, unless you were a co-applicant or guarantor. Loans taken by your husband in his name only don't affect your score.

Both of you have separate credit scores. However, if you're a joint account holder on a credit card or joint loan applicant, it affects both scores.

Check your individual credit reports to confirm what accounts are in your name.

faqs.question: Can I dispute a loan that was reported incorrectly to the bureau?
faqs.answer:
Yes. If a lender reported a loan/EMI incorrectly (wrong amount, wrong due date, marked as default when you paid on-time), file a dispute directly with the credit bureau.

Go to CIBIL/Experian/Equifax website → Dispute Section → Provide evidence (payment proof, bank statement, loan agreement). The bureau contacts the lender, who has 30 days to respond.

If lender can't prove their claim, the entry is removed from your report. Dispute is free.

faqs.question: What is the maximum CIBIL score?
faqs.answer:
900 is the maximum across all four Indian bureaus: CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark. All use the same 300-900 scale.

Nobody needs 900 though. Anything above 750 already unlocks the best loan and card offers, so chasing the ceiling adds nothing.

faqs.question: Is SBI CIBIL score check free on YONO?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Open YONO, go to Loans & Insurance, then Credit Score, and your real CIBIL number appears free.

It is the same TransUnion CIBIL score the bank uses internally, refreshed monthly. PNB One, HDFC, ICICI, and Axis apps have the same free feature.

faqs.question: Which is the official CIBIL score website?
faqs.answer:
cibil.com is the only official site, run by TransUnion CIBIL. The free score and report option sits behind the Get Free CIBIL Score & Report button.

Ignore lookalike sites asking for payment upfront. The annual report is free by RBI mandate and needs only PAN plus OTP verification.

faqs.question: CIBIL score kaise badhaye fastest?
faqs.answer:
Clear any overdue amount first: that alone recovers 30-50 points. Then pay every EMI and card bill on time and keep card utilization under 30%.

Avoid all new loan applications for 6 months. With clean behaviour, 80-150 points of recovery in 6-12 months is a realistic range.

disclaimer: Credit score information is based on RBI regulations and bureau practices as of March 2026. Scores, methodologies, and regulations may change. Always verify current information from official bureau websites.
